page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor and an NVIDIA L4 GPU. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under a KVM hypervisor, this instance features 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, requiring external storage attachments.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU metrics, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 402.56 tokens per second using a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing for the same model remains in the average tier.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside dedicated GPU acceleration, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring GPU-bound compute without needing massive multi-core CPU scaling. The shared CPU allocation and average multi-core benchmark results represent a tradeoff for CPU-heavy parallel processing. This configuration is suited for light LLM inference, machine learning development, single-threaded data processing, and GPU-accelerated rendering tasks.
